That is, if you translate it into good language: "Who doesn’t drink these days?" "Do we have anything to drink, Peter?"

16: I fell to thinking again. And strange was my thought. It was enveloped around something in such a way that it itself was enveloped in something. And that "something"’ was also strange. And my soul, my soul was heavy.
17: What was I doing just then, falling asleep or waking up? I don’t know, and how could I know? "There’s astate, but there’s no name for it, not sleep nor waking is it.’ I dozed like that for about twelve or thirty-five minutes.
18: And when I came to there wasn’t a soul in the car, and Peter had disappeared somewhere. The train continued to race through the rain and the blackness. It was strange to listen to the slamming of doors in all the cars, strange because there wasn’t a single soul in any of the cars.
19: I lay there like a corpse, in icy perspiration, and fear kept building under my heart.
21: Peter appeared in the door with a bluish, evil face. "Come over here, Peter, come over here. You're also all wet, why? That was you just now slamming the doors, right?"
22: "T wasn’t slamming anything. I was asleep."
24: Peter looked at me without blinking.
25: "Oh, that’s nothing, nothing. If alarm is growing under your heart, you've got to stifle it, and in order to stifle it, you've got to have a drink. But do we have anything to drink?"
27: "And isn’t there anyone at all in the whole world?"
29: ‘You're lying, Peter, you're always lying to me! If there isn’t anyone else, then who’s banging around with the doors and windows? Huh? Do you know? Do you hear? You've got something to drink, no doubt, and you keep lying to me!"’
30: Peter was looking at me, always the same, unblinking and spiteful. I saw by his ugly face that I had gotten to the core of him, that I understood him, and that now he feared me. Yes, yes, he had fiddled around with the candelabrum and put it out himself, and then went along through the car putting out the lights. "He’s ashamed, ashamed," I thought. But he had already jumped out the window.
31: I cried, "Come back, Peter,"’ in a voice even I couldn't recognize. "‘Come back!"’
32: ‘Trickster!’ he answered from behind the window.
33: And suddenly he flitted back into the car again and flew up to me, and tore at my hair with the most desperate spite.
34: "What’s with you, Peter? What’s with you?!’
35: ‘Nothing. Stay, stay on here, hag. Stay, old bitch! Go on to Moscow. Sell your seeds there. I can’t stand it, I can't st-a-a-and it."’
36: And once more he flitted away, this time for good.
37: ‘"The devil knows what’s up. What’s with the bunch of them?’ I squeezed my temples, shuddered and shook. The train shuddered and shook with me.
